title: What Is Fabric? for apparel sourcing for Apparel
meta_description: Fabric is cloth made by weaving, knitting, or otherwise forming yarns or fibers into a sheet used for apparel and home textiles.

title: Fabric vs Textile vs Cloth Fabric Notes Use Notes
meta_description: Cloth and fabric usually name the finished sheet. Textile is the broader word for fibers, yarns, and finished materials.

title: What Are Warp and Weft? Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Warp yarns run the length of a woven cloth. Weft yarns cross them. Together they make a weave. See how What Are Warp and Weft? relates to construction.

title: Fiber, Yarn, and Fabric Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Fiber is the raw strand, yarn is spun or extruded fiber, and fabric is the sheet made from yarn or fiber. See how Fiber, Yarn, and Fabric relates to.
H1: What is the difference between fiber, yarn, and fabric?

title: Polyester, Cotton, and Nylon Fabric Notes
meta_description: Polyester and nylon are synthetic filaments. Cotton is a plant fiber. Hand, moisture, and recovery depend on the cloth, not the name alone.
H1: How does polyester differ from cotton and nylon?

title: Fabrics for Hot Weather Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Hot-weather cloth is usually lighter and more open. Linen, cotton, and some cellulosics are common starts. No fiber is always the coolest.
H1: Which fabrics work in hot weather?

title: Fabrics for Winter Clothing Fabric Notes
meta_description: Winter cloth is chosen for structure, cover, and insulation. Wool and denser knits are common. Heavier is not automatically warmer.

title: What Is Tencel Lyocell? Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Lyocell is a regenerated cellulose fiber. Tencel is a branded lyocell. It starts from wood pulp and is processed, so it is not a raw natural fiber.

title: Chiffon, Organza, and Georgette Fabric Notes
meta_description: These are lightweight sheers used for dresses, overlays, and scarves. Organza is crisper. Georgette is drier. Chiffon is softer.
H1: What are chiffon, organza, and georgette used for?

title: What Is Thread Count? Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: Thread count counts yarns in a square inch of woven cloth. It is common in sheeting. It is not a universal quality score.

title: Does Thread Count Mean Better Fabric? for Apparel
meta_description: No. A higher thread count can mean a denser weave. Fiber, yarn size, and finish still decide whether the cloth is useful.
H1: Does a higher thread count always mean better fabric?

title: How to Identify Fabric Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: Start with the label, then hand, construction, and published composition. A photo alone does not identify a fiber. See how How to Identify Fabric.
H1: How can you identify a fabric?

title: What Is a Fabric Burn Test? Fabric Notes
meta_description: A burn test heats fiber and reads the residue. It is a fire hazard. FabStitch does not publish a procedure. Use a textile lab for commercial.
H1: What is a fabric burn test?

title: Resources for Identifying Fabric Fabric Notes
meta_description: Use the fabric record, construction guides, and a laboratory when composition is unknown. Do not treat a blog photo as a certificate.

title: Why Linen Wrinkles More Than Cotton Fabric Notes
meta_description: Flax fibers are stiffer and less elastic than cotton, so linen creases and holds the crease. That is characteristic, not automatically a defect.
H1: Why does linen wrinkle more than cotton?

title: Is Linen More Absorbent Than Cotton? for Apparel
meta_description: Linen is widely treated as a fast-wicking cloth. Cotton holds moisture in the fiber. The actual cloth and finish decide what you feel.
H1: Is linen more absorbent than cotton?

title: What Makes Lyocell Called Sustainable? Use Notes
meta_description: Lyocell starts from wood pulp and is spun in a solvent process designed to recover that solvent. The claim still depends on sourcing and certification.
H1: What makes Tencel or lyocell described as sustainable?

title: What Is Organic Cotton? Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Organic cotton is cotton grown under an organic farming standard. GOTS is one textile standard. A cotton page is not organic unless the record says so.

title: What OEKO-TEX Standard 100 Means Fabric Notes
meta_description: OEKO-TEX Standard 100 means a textile was tested for harmful substances against that standard's limits. It is not an organic label and not a quality.

title: Which Fabrics Are Called Eco-Friendly? Use Notes
meta_description: Organic cotton, lyocell, hemp, and some recycled fibers are often discussed. Each claim needs a scope. No fiber is impact-free.

title: Fabric Eco-Labels Explained Fabric Notes
meta_description: GOTS covers organic textile processing. OEKO-TEX Standard 100 covers harmful substances. A label applies only when that cloth is certified.

title: What Is Satin? for apparel sourcing Fabric Notes
meta_description: Satin is a weave with floats that make a smooth face. It can be silk, polyester, or another fiber. It is not itself a fiber.

title: Caring for Delicate Fabrics Fabric Notes
meta_description: Silk, wool, velvet, and sheers do not share one wash cycle. Follow the cloth or garment label. This page does not replace it.
H1: How should delicate fabrics be cared for?

title: Personal Fabric Stash Marketplaces Fabric Notes
meta_description: Peer resale boards are not the same as a B2B fabric marketplace. FabStitch is for discovering documented cloth, not trading leftover stashes.
H1: Is there a marketplace for personal fabric stashes?

title: What Is Fabric MOQ? for apparel sourcing
meta_description: MOQ is the supplier's minimum order. FabStitch does not publish one minimum for every cloth. Ask on the fabric you actually want.

title: How to Request Fabric Samples Fabric Notes
meta_description: Request a sample against a specific fabric page, with end use and quantity. FabStitch does not run a separate overseas sample checkout.
H1: How do businesses request fabric samples?

title: How to Verify Fabric Quality Fabric Notes
meta_description: Read composition and construction, compare like with like, and test when the risk is commercial. A catalog photo is not a test report.
H1: How can a buyer verify fabric quality?

title: Sourcing Sustainable or Technical Cloth Use Notes
meta_description: Look for documented fiber, construction, and any real certificate. FabStitch does not run a separate technical-fabric portal.
H1: How do buyers source sustainable or technical fabrics?

title: Upholstery and Bedding Fabrics Fabric Notes
meta_description: Upholstery wants abrasion resistance. Bedding wants next-to-skin hand. They are not one cloth, and car seats are a different specification.
H1: Which fabrics suit upholstery or bedding?

title: Why Wool Care Labels Differ Fabric Notes
meta_description: The same fiber name can hide a different knit, finish, or blend. Follow each garment label. Do not average them. See how Why Wool Care Labels Differ.
H1: Why can two wool sweaters have different ironing labels?

title: How Cotton Hand Softens Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Cotton hand comes from yarn, finish, and washing. There is no sure-fire home recipe that is safe for every cotton. See how How Cotton Hand Softens.

title: Faded Lines on Jeans Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: Indigo sits near the yarn surface. Creases and abrasion lose colour first. A wash line is wear, not a GSM fault. See how Faded Lines on Jeans relates.
H1: What causes faded lines on jeans after washing?

title: Judging Thread in a Garment Fabric Notes
meta_description: Look at the seam, the fiber of the thread, and whether it matches the cloth. Thread count of the fabric is a different number.
H1: How can thread quality in a garment be judged?

title: What Is Cork Fabric? Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: Cork fabric is cork sheet on a backing, used for small goods more than for draped apparel. FabStitch does not list it as a catalog family.

title: Outdoor Upholstery Cloth for Apparel for Apparel
meta_description: Outdoor upholstery is built for weather and rub, often with coatings that reduce breathability. It is not automatically suitable for apparel.
H1: Can outdoor upholstery fabric be used for clothes?

title: How to Choose a Fabric Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: Choose from the garment, then construction, then fiber. Confidence comes from a written brief, not from guessing a colour story.
H1: How do you choose a fabric?

title: What Is Aida Cloth? for apparel sourcing
meta_description: Aida is an evenweave grid used for counted cross-stitch. It is not an apparel fabric in the FabStitch catalog. See how What Is Aida Cloth? relates to.

title: Everyday Laundry Mistakes Fabric Notes Use Notes
meta_description: Heat, mixing unfinished dyes, and ignoring the label cause most everyday damage. Care is per cloth, not one cycle for the wardrobe.

title: Chiffon, Georgette, and Satin Fabric Notes
meta_description: Chiffon and georgette are sheers with different hands. Satin is a smooth weave. Fiber is a separate question. See how Chiffon, Georgette, and Satin.
H1: How do chiffon, georgette, and satin differ?

title: Voile and Cotton for apparel sourcing for Apparel
meta_description: Voile is usually a lightweight plain-weave cloth. Cotton is a fiber. Cotton voile is both. They are not opposing materials.
H1: What is the difference between voile and cotton?

title: Fabric Stains: Oil, Wine, and Makeup for Apparel
meta_description: Blot, then follow the care label. Oil, wine, and makeup are different soils. No home recipe is safe for every cloth. See how Fabric Stains: Oil, Wine.
H1: How should fabric stains be approached?

title: Fabrics and Sweat for apparel sourcing Use Notes
meta_description: Open cloths and some performance knits move moisture differently. No fiber guarantees dry skin. Compare construction. See how Fabrics and Sweat relates
H1: Which fabrics do not trap sweat?
primary_topic: fabrics that do not trap sweat

title: Identifying Georgette and Satin Fabric Notes
meta_description: Georgette is a drier sheer. Satin has a smooth, light-catching face. The fiber still has to be read from the label. See how Identifying Georgette and.
H1: How do you tell georgette from satin?

title: Buying Fabric by Metre or Yard Fabric Notes
meta_description: Order length and read width separately. One yard is 0.9144 metres. Yield still depends on the pattern and the cloth width.
H1: How do you buy fabric by length?

title: Choosing Woven Wool or Cotton Fabric Notes
meta_description: Pick the garment climate first. Wool wovens often structure tailoring. Cotton wovens cover shirts through denser twills.
H1: How do you choose a woven wool or cotton?

title: How to Read Fabric Prints Fabric Notes Use Notes
meta_description: Judge a print by the ground cloth, the placement, and colourfastness. FabStitch does not publish a 2026 trend ranking. See how How to Read Fabric.
H1: How should a buyer read fabric prints?

title: What Is Ripstop Fabric? Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Ripstop is a weave with thicker yarns at intervals so a tear is slower to run. It is common in bags and outer layers. It is not a shoe system.
H1: What is ripstop fabric used for?

title: Microfiber and Rayon Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: Microfiber is a very fine synthetic filament, often polyester. Rayon is regenerated cellulose, usually viscose. They are different families.
H1: How do microfiber and rayon differ?

title: Cloth for Structured Jackets Fabric Notes
meta_description: Structured jackets start with a stable weave: wool, cotton twill, or a documented blend. Decorative borders are a separate trim spec.

title: Fabrics for Zippers and Buttons Fabric Notes
meta_description: Fasteners need a stable ground. Sheers and loose knits often need reinforcement. No fiber is the zipper fabric. See how Fabrics for Zippers and Buttons
H1: Which fabrics hold zippers and buttons?

title: Fabrics for Children's Clothing Fabric Notes
meta_description: Soft hand, documented composition, and washability matter. No fiber is the softest or the safest for every child. See how Fabrics for Children's.
H1: What should buyers consider for children's clothing?

title: Why Fabric Color Fades Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: Light, wash, rub, and dye class move colour. Printed and dyed cloth can both fade. No home method locks every dye. See how Why Fabric Color Fades.

title: Why Seams Pucker for apparel sourcing for Apparel
meta_description: Pucker is the cloth gathering at the seam. Match needle and tension to the cloth, and stabilize sheers. This is not a machine manual.

title: New Cloth and Worn Cloth Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Wear relaxes finish, fades colour, and can pill or shine a cloth. New and worn are not two quality grades. See how New Cloth and Worn Cloth relates to.
H1: How does new fabric differ from worn fabric?

title: Crepe de Chine and Georgette Fabric Notes
meta_description: No. Crepe de chine is a tighter, smoother crepe. Georgette is sheerer and drier. Both can be silk or synthetic. See how Crepe de Chine and Georgette.
H1: Are crepe de chine and georgette the same?

title: Lining Fabrics for apparel sourcing Fabric Notes
meta_description: Linings are chosen for slip, weight, and heat. Viscose and some silks are common. Leather styling is not a lining standard.
H1: What lining cloth should a brief name?

title: Storing Clothes for apparel sourcing for Apparel
meta_description: Store clean, dry cloth. Fold knits. Hang structured wovens if the cloth can take it. Storage does not remove stains. See how Storing Clothes relates to

title: Caring for Hand-Dyed Fabric Fabric Notes
meta_description: Assume a hand dye may crock until a wash test says otherwise. Wash it alone, cool, and do not promise colourfastness. See how Caring for Hand-Dyed.
H1: How should hand-dyed fabric be cared for?

title: Digital Prints and Reverse Prints Fabric Notes
meta_description: A digital print is applied from a file onto cloth. Reverse print is not one standard. Ask which face carries the ink. See how Digital Prints and.
H1: What is a digital print versus a reverse print?

title: Tencel and Viscose for apparel sourcing Use Notes
meta_description: Both are regenerated cellulose. Lyocell uses a solvent-spinning process. Viscose uses a different chemical route. They are not polyester.
H1: How do Tencel lyocell and viscose differ?

title: Fabric and Skin Comfort Fabric Notes for Apparel
meta_description: Comfort is hand, finish, and friction. No fiber is medically skin-safe for everyone. Sample if the wearer is sensitive. See how Fabric and Skin Comfort
H1: Which fabrics are comfortable against skin?

title: Durable Fiber Blends Fabric Notes Fabric Notes
meta_description: No blend wins every test. Durability is abrasion, seam, and use. A cotton-polyester twill and a wool blend answer different jobs.
H1: Which fiber blend is most durable?
